title: Capacity Gating Framework and SLA Choice Matrix for Enterprise Dedicated Requests
creator: Evelyn Park
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a deterministic intake and gating framework for enterprise dedicated capacity requests that sets SLA targets, maps reserved throughput to GPU class, and prescribes scaling policies (autoscale/burst/preemption) per customer profile. Goal is to reduce manual back-and-forth during onboarding, speed time-to-commit, and surface cost/availability trade-offs to sales and CS in a reproducible way.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals: 1) Create an SLA choice matrix (latency SLO, p95/p99 targets, throughput slots) tied to accepted GPU families and quantization profiles; 2) Define reserved throughput buckets and corresponding autoscale/burst rules; 3) Provide a deterministic gating rubric for capacity approvals (cost threshold, compliance reqs, region constraints, data residency).
- Non-goals: Full automation of provisioning (handled in ENG workstream), negotiate individual enterprise price terms.

Acceptance criteria:
- SLA choice matrix doc exists (Confluence link) mapping three customer tiers (Baseline, Performance, Dedicated-Enterprise) to latency p95/p99, throughput (tokens/sec), and recommended GPU class.
- Intake form updated in console intake flow with required fields (workload profile, peak qps, max latency, retention, compliance needs).
- Playbook section with runbook for CS/sales describing gating yes/no rules and escalation steps when a request falls outside standard buckets.
- A/B test plan for rollout with 10 initial customers to validate sizing and cost predictions.

Proposed SLA choice matrix (high-level):
- Baseline (SLA: best-effort): p95 <= 500ms, p99 <= 800ms, reserved throughput: 0-50k tokens/min, GPU class: T4 / A10 compatible; autoscale: opportunistic.
- Performance (SLA: commercial): p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms, reserved throughput: 50k-250k tokens/min, GPU class: A10 / A100-40GB, autoscale with bounded burst to 1.5x reserved.
- Dedicated-Enterprise (SLA: enterprise): p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 220ms, reserved throughput: >250k tokens/min, GPU class: A100-80GB or H100-80GB, guaranteed reserved pools with burst policy and preemption protections.

Scaling policies and constraints:
- Autoscale window sizes, warm pool sizing, and KV cache priming rules are delegated to ENG; product must define the customer-visible knobs and maximum permitted burst multiplier.
- For GPUs with limited availability (H100), provide fallback GPU classes with transparent performance delta and automatic routing.

Trade-offs and decisions to be made in review:
- Whether to tie reserved throughput strictly to GPU family or allow a performance SLA + price estimation and leave mapping to runtime (more flexibility vs predictability).
- Whether to expose a custom latency SLA for individual customers (adds negotiation overhead).

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/DEDT-Intake (draft)
- Intake form prototype (Figma): https://drive.google.com/figma/d/enterprise-intake
- Cost model spreadsheet (internal): https://drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/Capacity-Sizing-Model
- Related Linear tickets: PM-33107 (capacity scorecard), ENG-8421 (autoscale runtime work)

Risks:
- Overly strict GPU mapping will increase time-to-onboard for customers with specialized hardware needs.
- If reserved throughput buckets are too coarse, estimates will be frequently revised and increase operational churn.

Rollout plan:
1) Finalize matrix and intake form (this ticket).
2) Run intake with 10 pilot enterprise customers (2 weeks).
3) Measure accuracy of throughput predictions and SLA compliance; adjust buckets.
4) Publish official Dedicated intake guide for sales/CS and add to console intake UX.

Metrics to evaluate success:
- Time from intake submission to committed reservation (target < 7 business days for standard buckets).
- % of pilot customers meeting SLA in 30 days (target >= 85%).
- Number of manual escalations required during triage (target <= 2 per 10 pilots).
